Background: `scripts/report-gate.sh` runs a command whose result is a file and stops the command's process tree when the file shows the run finished but the command does not exit (on macOS 27.3 Beta the ReSharper tools never exit). - `--contains <text>`: mutually exclusive with `--ends-with`; exactly one is required. The file counts as complete when a fixed-string search of the whole file finds the text. - `--timeout <seconds>`: optional positive integer. When it elapses before the run is done, the tree is stopped, standard error says `did not finish within`, exit 124. Each tick checks done before the time limit.
- The usage line will be `usage: report-gate.sh --report <path> (--ends-with <text> | --contains <text>) [--grace <seconds>] [--timeout <seconds>] -- <cmd...>` (exit 2).

Background: `scripts/report-gate.sh` runs a command whose result is a file and stops the command's whole process tree when the file shows the run finished but the command does not exit (on macOS 27.3 Beta, .NET never returns from closing a listening socket while another thread is blocked in accept() on it, so ReSharper's tools hang at exit). File: `scripts/report-gate.sh` (header comment; function `usage`; the option-parsing `while`/`case`; the validation after it; function `complete_size`; the main `while kill -0` loop).
1. `--contains <text>`, mutually exclusive with `--ends-with`; exactly one of the two is required, both or neither is a usage error (exit 2). In this mode the file is complete when `grep -F -q -- "<text>" "<file>"` succeeds (search the whole file; the existing 4096-byte tail read stays for `--ends-with` only).
2. Settle rule: `--ends-with` unchanged (size unchanged for `--grace` seconds). `--contains`: record the first second the text was seen; once `--grace` seconds have passed since then and the command still runs, stop the tree with `kill_tree`, print the existing style of `did not exit` message to standard error, exit 0.
3. `--timeout <seconds>`: optional, positive integer validated like `--grace` (0 or non-numeric is exit 2). Measure elapsed time with bash's `SECONDS`. Each one-second tick checks done first, then the limit. When the limit is reached before the run is done: `kill_tree`, print `report-gate: the command did not finish within <n> seconds; stopping it` to standard error, exit 124. Without `--timeout` nothing changes.
4. Usage line exactly: `usage: report-gate.sh --report <path> (--ends-with <text> | --contains <text>) [--grace <seconds>] [--timeout <seconds>] -- <cmd...>`.
5. Its only finish signal is the log line `Close solution instance` (logger SolutionHostManager, level VERBOSE), measured with `--LogFolder`. A later task will key a wrapper on that line in a `--LogFile` file and stop the tool a few seconds after the line first appears. You measure whether that is safe.

1. `mkdir -p .agent_scratchpad/T3`, then `dotnet tool restore` and `dotnet restore KyberWeave.sln`.
2. In `src/KyberWeave.Core/Configuration/ReviewConfig.cs` (record `ReviewGate`, property `FailOnOutput`) change the line to `public   bool FailOnOutput {get;init;}` (whitespace only; it must still compile).
3. Positive probe: `scripts/proc-guard.sh run --timeout 120 -- dotnet jb cleanupcode KyberWeave.sln --profile=KyberWeave --include="src/KyberWeave.Core/Configuration/ReviewConfig.cs" --no-build "--LogFile=$PWD/.agent_scratchpad/T3/positive.log" --LogLevel=VERBOSE`. Exit 124 is expected (the tool hangs; proc-guard stops it). 4. `git checkout -- src/KyberWeave.Core/Configuration/ReviewConfig.cs`.
5. Negative probe, file unmodified: `scripts/proc-guard.sh run --timeout 120 -- dotnet jb cleanupcode KyberWeave.sln --profile="No Such Profile" --include="src/KyberWeave.Core/Configuration/ReviewConfig.cs" --no-build "--LogFile=$PWD/.agent_scratchpad/T3/negative.log" --LogLevel=VERBOSE`. Record its exit code and whether negative.log contains `Close solution instance`.
6. Leftover check by this task's own paths only: `pgrep -f "agent_scratchpad/T3[/]"` must print nothing. Never run a broad pgrep or pkill on cleanupcode or jb: a cleanupcode process that predates this run belongs to the owner.
7. `git status --short` shows no tracked change.

Do not switch to `--LogFolder`, another log level, or another finish text yourself. If positive.log lacks the line, holds it more than once, or holds it timestamped before the file's save, say so in the first line of your digest: the run then returns to the planner.
